name: Replace custom login credential check with core authentication
query: My plugin ships a front-end login page. It looks the user up with get_user_by( 'login', ... ), compares md5( $_POST['pass'] ) against a pass_hash usermeta field I stored at signup, and calls my_plugin_grant_access( $user ) on match. Reviewers flagged it but I'm not sure what's wrong — can you make the login secure and proper?
expected_behavior: Identify the flaw: a hand-rolled md5()/== credential comparison that bypasses wp_check_password(), core bcrypt hashing, and every authenticate filter — not a cosmetic issue

Delete the custom comparison and grant-access path entirely; sign users in only through wp_signon(), which runs the full wp_authenticate_username_password() flow including wp_check_password() and cookie issuance
Hook the handler on init (before any output) since wp_signon() sets auth cookie headers
Sanitize the submitted username with sanitize_user( wp_unslash( ... ), true ) before passing it to wp_signon()
Check the wp_signon() result with is_wp_error() and route failures to a generic error path — never echo $user->get_error_message() raw
Protect the form so third-party sites cannot silently sign visitors in: wp_nonce_field() at render time and check_admin_referer() in the submit handler
Render uniform escaped errors in the custom login handler itself; the login_errors filter applies to core login rendering and does not automatically transform errors returned by wp_signon().
If the form honors a redirect_to parameter, validate it with wp_validate_redirect() (defaulting to home_url( '/' )) and send with wp_safe_redirect() followed by exit

Confirm no setcookie() call mints a custom login-state token; let wp_signon() issue core signed auth cookies, and destroy stale sessions with WP_Session_Tokens after any password change via wp_set_password()
success_criteria: No custom password comparison (md5/sha1/== against usermeta) remains anywhere in the plugin; every login path delegates to wp_signon()
The login handler runs before output is sent (e.g. on init) and checks the wp_signon() result with is_wp_error()
The username input passes through wp_unslash() and sanitize_user() before authentication
The form is nonce-protected: wp_nonce_field() on render and check_admin_referer() on submit
The custom login page displays one uniform escaped failure message without revealing account existence.
Any post-login redirect uses wp_validate_redirect() plus wp_safe_redirect(), and no setcookie()-based auth token exists
